items: Is the program live right now (not suspended or closed)?
Is entry free — no submission fee, no paid tier required?
Is it open to a new researcher — no invite, no reputation minimum?
Does filing need IDV/KYC first? If yes, is the ID valid and unexpired?
Is testing restricted (testnet-only, test accounts only, never another real person's account)?
Is the scope clear — what is in scope and what is explicitly excluded?
Are payout terms stated (amounts, currency, KYC/KYB for payout)?
First report only, or can others file the same finding?
If any gate fails, record the verdict (PASS / CAUTION / FAIL) and the exact gate — do not file anyway.
title: Program triage checklist

items: Are the exact reproduction commands listed (copy-paste, not described)?
Is the environment stated (version, commit, OS, tool versions)?
Is there a control — the same input without the trigger, showing the expected (safe) result?
Expected vs actual output — both shown, with the full log pasted inline?
Is the PoC reproducible from a clean state in about a minute?
Are evidence files attached (logs, test source, config) — never 'available on request'?
Does the PoC avoid running payloads against live users or production?
Are limits stated honestly (what was NOT tested)?
title: PoC verification checklist

items: Test only on testnet, or on your own accounts — never another real person's account.
Mainnet/production testing disqualifies on some programs — read the rules first.
Never handle or share private keys, seed phrases, or session tokens.
Simulate before every state-changing transaction; stop on any revert.
Never submit a report, move funds, or sign anything on behalf of the site.
Never run exploit code or payloads against live users.
Keep findings confidential until triaged — do not publish unfiled or in-triage findings.
Verify every claim live before reporting it; screenshots beat memory.
title: Safe-testing rules

items: Is the contract source verified on the explorer?
Who is the owner — and can ownership be transferred or renounced?
Can the owner mint, pause, withdraw, blacklist, or upgrade? (read the ABI)
Is there a honeypot or mint-simulation flag? Simulate a buy and a sell.
Holder distribution — how concentrated are the top holders?
Is the liquidity pool locked, and for how long?
Does the contract have a proxy/upgrade path? Who controls it?
Report each item pass / fail / unknown with evidence. Never claim a hidden vulnerability.
title: Contract audit checklist (public, read-only)
